site.title: Lyα — from gas to forest · science notes
site.about: An interactive teaching resource on how neutral hydrogen between a distant quasar and us becomes the Lyman-α forest: atoms meet light, light stretches, gas maps to velocity, optical depth adds, transmitted light multiplies, and the forest can be read backward only up to a point. These notes list, for every scientific claim the scenes make, its sources, the assumptions under which it holds, the simplifications made for teaching, and how the browser's numbers were checked.
modeled: Lyman-α absorption by neutral hydrogen: the 1s → 2p resonance [[#lya-transition-data|Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data]], met in each atom's own frame [[#doppler-resonance-condition|Resonance in the atom's frame (Doppler condition)]], removes light from the beam by scattering it in other directions [[#resonant-scattering|Lyα "absorption" in the IGM is resonant scattering out of the beam]].

Line shapes: thermal Doppler broadening [[#thermal-doppler-broadening|Doppler parameter and the thermal (Gaussian) profile]], natural broadening from the lifetime of the 2p level [[#natural-broadening|Natural broadening from the finite lifetime of 2p]], and their combination, the Voigt profile [[#voigt-profile|The Voigt profile — normalisation, definition and asymptotics]].

From gas to spectrum: cosmological redshift [[#cosmological-redshift|Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor]]; the map from real space to velocity space, u = aH(z)·x + v_pec [[#real-to-velocity-mapping|Real space → velocity space map]]; optical depth accumulated along the sightline [[#optical-depth-accumulation|Line-of-sight accumulation of optical depth in velocity space]], which adds [[#optical-depths-add|Why optical depths add]]; and transmitted flux F = e^−τ [[#beer-lambert|Transmitted flux (Beer–Lambert)]], which saturates [[#saturation-curve-of-growth|Saturation and the curve of growth]].

Observation and inference: a spectrograph's resolution and noise act on the recorded flux [[#instrument-resolution|Instrument resolution acts on the observed flux]] [[#noise-model|Noise model and signal-to-noise]]; several arrangements of gas can record the same line [[#same-shadow-degeneracy|The "same shadow" configurations]], and further information can break the tie [[#breaking-the-degeneracy|What breaks the degeneracy]].
not_modeled: No hydrodynamics. The gas is a toy Zel'dovich volume [[#toy-volume|The toy Zel'dovich volume (synthetic teaching data)]], not an evolved simulation: temperature follows a power-law temperature–density relation and the velocities follow linear theory; nothing is computed from a thermal or dynamical history.

Neutral hydrogen is set by photoionisation equilibrium in a uniform ultraviolet background [[#photoionisation-equilibrium|Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control]]. There is no transfer of ionising radiation, no self-shielding and no collisional ionisation; the scene that changes the neutral amount holds density and temperature fixed.

One velocity and one temperature per sampling element [[#unresolved-velocity-structure|One velocity per sampling element (unresolved velocity structure is not represented)]]: velocity structure smaller than a cell is not represented.

Only Lyman-α is drawn, except in the last scene, where Lyman-β and a heavier-ion line appear as extra information. There is no continuum fitting, no quasar proximity effect, and the fine structure of Lyman-α is below every width shown [[#lya-transition-data|Lyα (H I 1s → 2p) transition data]].

Teaching representations are marked as such where they appear: atoms are a representative sample [[#representative-atoms|Representative atoms are a cartoon sample]], parcels are a decomposition of a continuous sightline [[#teaching-parcels|Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline]], and the natural width is magnified wherever it is drawn [[#magnified-natural-width|Natural width is magnified wherever it is drawn]].

toy_vs_real.text: Every scene draws from one small synthetic data set: a 20 Mpc/h Zel'dovich volume at z = 3 (a 20 × 8 × 8 Mpc/h block of it is drawn) and one sightline through it [[#toy-volume|The toy Zel'dovich volume (synthetic teaching data)]], decomposed for teaching into parcels and cells [[#teaching-parcels|Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline]]. It is not a hydrodynamic simulation and contains no data from any survey or simulation suite.

Independent calculations check the browser's physics: SciPy's Faddeeva function for the Voigt profile, exact-Voigt optical-depth sums, numerical integration of distances, and the fake_spectra code for the real-space method. Their results are listed under Accuracy.

The skewer interface [[#skewer-interface|The skewer interface (dataset-independent)]] is independent of the data set, so a later release may replace the toy with simulation skewers whose conventions match fake_spectra [[#fake-spectra-conventions|fake_spectra conventions (the validation reference)]]. No such data are included in this release.

chapters.intro: Why optical depths add while transmitted light multiplies, what saturation does, and what an instrument changes — the record, not the gas.

SCI-RED-001.title: Cosmological redshift stretches every wavelength by the same factor
SCI-RED-001.claim: Light absorbed by gas at redshift z_abs at rest-frame wavelength λ_rest (1215.67 Å for Lyα, in the gas's own frame) reaches us at λ_obs = λ_rest (1 + z_abs), where 1 + z_abs = a(t_obs)/a(t_abs). Every wavelength, and every wavelength interval, is multiplied by the same factor. The reverse operation, λ_rest = λ_obs/(1 + z_abs), re-expresses the observed spectrum in the absorber's rest frame: there the absorber's own line is at exactly 1215.67 Å. (In the quasar's rest frame, λ_obs/(1 + z_q), the same absorption lies blueward of 1215.67 Å — [[#quasar-rest-frame|The quasar's frame — why the forest lies blueward of the quasar's own Lyα]].)

SCI-RED-001.convention: Three frames are kept distinct: the absorber's rest frame (where the atom sees 1215.67 Å), the observer's frame (us), and the quasar's rest frame ([[#quasar-rest-frame|The quasar's frame — why the forest lies blueward of the quasar's own Lyα]]). "Measured at a point along the path" means by an observer at rest with the cosmic expansion there (comoving), for whom λ ∝ a.
assumptions: FLRW expansion; comoving observers; the gas's own small motion folded into z_abs here
SCI-RED-001.validity: any z; the beat uses 0 ≤ z_abs < z_q = 3.2 with z = 3 as the default (the toy's redshift)
simplifications: Redshift is presented as the stretching of the light's wavelength with the expansion (λ ∝ a); the Doppler-vs-expansion interpretation debate is not raised.

SCI-DEG-001.title: The "same shadow" configurations
SCI-DEG-001.claim: A constructed degeneracy example, not a model of typical forest absorbers: (i) one unusually hot, idealised compact gas clump (T = 4.5×10⁴ K, Hubble width 2.23 km/s — about 7 kpc proper, far more compact than typical forest gas — N = 2.5×10¹⁴, at rest); (ii) two cold clouds (T = 10⁴ K, Hubble width 12.8 km/s each, 78 km/s apart in Hubble flow, 9.75×10¹³ each, approaching at ±24.9 km/s); (iii) one cold cloud stretched along the line (T = 10⁴ K, Hubble width 11.15 km/s, N = 2.5×10¹⁴) whose smooth extra velocity across 1σ (5.988 km/s) is computed from (i), not tuned: it is the value that gives (iii) the same total Doppler parameter as (i), b_tot² = 2kT/m_H + 2σ_u² = (27.431 km/s)², with the same column. At S/N = 20 per 2.5 km/s pixel with perfect resolution the three Lyα lines are not significantly distinguishable (Δχ² ≈ 2.8 for the blend over 121 pixels); the blend shows by S/N = 50 (Δχ² ≈ 17) and grows as (S/N)², while (iii) stays at Δχ² ≤ 0.002 at every S/N up to 200, in Lyα and in Lyβ. In this constructed model (i) and (iii) are degenerate in every H I Lyman-series line: for a Gaussian clump with a smooth (linear) velocity field the H I profile is a Voigt profile fixed by b_tot and N alone. These are two different kinds of degeneracy. The blend (ii) is measurement-limited: higher S/N, resolution or wavelength coverage can break it. Heat against smooth motion, (i) against (iii), is information-limited for hydrogen: every H I line depends only on the line-of-sight distribution of velocity and optical depth, in which thermal and smooth bulk broadening of one species are the same Gaussian, so another H I line gives no independent distinction — a line of a different mass does ([[#breaking-the-degeneracy|What breaks the degeneracy]]). The blend hides because its two components overlap inside the saturated Lyα core, where the transmitted flux is near zero however the optical depth is split ([[#saturation-curve-of-growth|Saturation and the curve of growth]]); Lyβ, with a smaller f λ, is not saturated there and separates it ([[#breaking-the-degeneracy|What breaks the degeneracy]]). What remains of (iii)'s difference is numerical: the clumps are cut at ±5σ (exact-Voigt path, max |ΔF| 4e-06), and the app adds its Voigt approximation's own error (max |ΔF| 4e-05; [[#voigt-numerics|Numerical Voigt implementation in the app]]).

SCI-REP-003.title: Parcels are a teaching decomposition of a continuous sightline
SCI-REP-003.claim: The three parcels a, b, c summarise three n_HI peak regions of the real toy sightline (HI-weighted position, width, column, temperature, velocity and gradient). They are not discrete clouds; Beat 8 dissolves them back into cells. A parcel has a size along the beam, so the velocity spread across it widens its line too (the physics is [[#velocity-gradient-broadening|Velocity-gradient (Hubble) broadening of an extended absorber]]). Beat 6 isolates the declared terms by setting the parcel's own peculiar-velocity gradient to zero (dv/dx = 0 there), so its size term is the Hubble flow alone, b_size = √2·aH·σ_x; for the parcel it starts from, b_size = 23.8 km/s against a thermal 21.4 km/s, so the drawn line is 32.0 km/s wide (b) — Beat 6's figure names both parts, and "show the physics" prints each and the drawn line's own width. SCI-REP-005.title: Ink is optical depth, and the ink rendering performs Beer–Lambert
SCI-REP-005.claim: "Ink" has one meaning throughout: a contribution to optical depth τ, laid in velocity space (Beats 6–13); neutral atoms are drawn as dark dots and motions as arrows, never called ink. The ribbon is rendered by compositing ink layers of opacity 1 − e^(−τᵢ) over a backlight C₀, which yields the transmitted fraction (C − C_ink)/(C₀ − C_ink) = Π e^(−τᵢ) = e^(−Στᵢ): the picture performs the rule it teaches (checked pixel by pixel, [[#check-rend-001|The drawing performs Beer–Lambert]]).

assumptions: ink colour ≈ black

SCI-REP-006.title: Four representations of the same gas, never mixed silently

Simulation particles are never drawn.

SCI-REP-007.title: The stretching ribbon and the written shadows (Beat 5 representation)
SCI-REP-007.claim: In Beat 5 the quasar's light is a ribbon carrying its own labels (the wavelength each part left with), laid against a ruler of wavelength measured where the light is now, starting at 0 Å, so the stretch by (1 + z_q)/(1 + z_here) is drawn exactly (anchored at zero, every interval scaled). Lyα of the gas being passed is a fixed mark at 1215.67 Å. The gas along the line of sight is a schematic continuous field, not a set of separate clouds: a seeded Gaussian random field in ln Δ (correlation length ~7 Mpc/h comoving, σ = 0.9; far coarser than real structure, chosen to be visible on a 4.5 Gpc/h path), quieter near the quasar, with three density peaks set exactly for the narration (the selected one, placed where the toy stretch's deepest absorption falls on the forest's own wavelength scale, so its shadow has the same wavelength in Beats 5, 11 and 12; and z = 2.90, 2.81). Every cell writes at its own Lyα with strength ∝ Δ² (photoionisation equilibrium, [[#photoionisation-equilibrium|Photoionisation equilibrium and the neutral-amount control]]) × ((1+z)/4)^1.6, normalised so ⟨F⟩ = 0.74 over z = 2–3; the forest therefore thins toward low z. Density peaks (Δ > 2.2, with their surroundings Δ > 1.3) are the "structures" the narration names and the reader can select. What each cell writes is drawn ~60× wider than a real forest line (6 Å Doppler width when written, versus ~0.1 Å for b = 25 km/s); shadows combine by Beer–Lambert. The close-up of the mark is magnified ~20×. The surface spectrum is continuum-normalised; the quasar's Lyα emission (a schematic bump) is drawn only with "show the physics". The light packet's drawn wavelength is proportional to its true stretch. Path positions are comoving distances ([[#comoving-distance|Comoving distance along the light's path (Planck 2018)]]).

validation.independent: the analytic Doppler parameter ([[#check-tau-001|Optical depth]]) and an independent Python implementation

python.snippet:
import numpy as np

k_B = 1.380649e-16      # Boltzmann constant, erg/K (exact, SI 2019)
m_H = 1.6735328e-24     # mass of the 1H atom, g (1.00782503223 u, NIST)

def b_thermal(T):
    """Doppler parameter of the thermal (Gaussian) profile, km/s: b = sqrt(2 k_B T / m_H)"""
    return np.sqrt(2 * k_B * T / m_H) / 1e5

for T in (4.0e3, 1.0e4, 4.2e4):
    print(f"T = {T:7.0f} K  ->  b = {b_thermal(T):.3f} km/s")

python.snippet:
import numpy as np
from scipy.special import wofz

k_B, m_H = 1.380649e-16, 1.6735328e-24
sigma_v = 2.6540e-2 * 0.4164 * 1215.6701e-8 / 1e5       # Lya: (pi e^2 / m_e c) f lambda0, cm^2 km/s
gamma = 6.2649e8 * 1215.6701e-8 / (4 * np.pi) / 1e5      # km/s
lyb = 0.079142 * 1025.72221 / (0.4164 * 1215.6701)       # Lyb optical depth relative to Lya: (f lambda) ratio
b_T = lambda T: np.sqrt(2 * k_B * T / m_H) / 1e5         # thermal Doppler parameter, km/s

# gases in velocity space: centre u, Hubble-flow width su (1 sigma), bulk velocity v, extra smooth velocity dv across 1 sigma
I = [dict(u=0.0, su=2.23, N=2.5e14, T=45000.0, v=0.0, dv=0.0)]                       # one hot, compact clump
II = [dict(u=-39.0, su=12.8, N=9.75e13, T=1e4, v=24.9, dv=0.0),                      # two cold clumps, converging
      dict(u=39.0, su=12.8, N=9.75e13, T=1e4, v=-24.9, dv=0.0)]
dv = np.sqrt(2.23**2 + (b_T(45000.0)**2 - b_T(1e4)**2) / 2) - 11.15                 # matching: b_T^2 + 2 sigma_u^2 equal
III = [dict(u=0.0, su=11.15, N=2.5e14, T=1e4, v=0.0, dv=dv)]                         # one cold clump, expanding

u = np.linspace(-150, 150, 121)                                                      # 2.5 km/s pixels
s = np.linspace(-5, 5, 401); w = np.exp(-s**2 / 2); w /= w.sum()                    # a clump in sub-cells over +-5 sigma
def tau(gas, scale=1.0):                       # no closed form here: every sub-cell is a thermal line at its own velocity
    t = np.zeros_like(u)
    for c in gas:
        b = b_T(c['T']); x = (u[:, None] - c['u'] - c['v'] - (c['su'] + c['dv']) * s) / b
        t += scale * c['N'] * sigma_v * (w * wofz(x + 1j * gamma / b).real).sum(1) / (np.sqrt(np.pi) * b)
    return t

sig3 = lambda x: f"{float(f'{x:.3g}'):g}"
print(f"(iii)'s smooth extra velocity from the matching condition: dv = {dv:.4f} km/s")
for line, scale in (("Lya", 1.0), ("Lyb", lyb)):
    F = {k: np.exp(-tau(g, scale)) for k, g in (("i", I), ("ii", II), ("iii", III))}
    for snr in (20, 50, 100, 200):
        chi2 = {k: np.sum((F[k] - F["i"]) ** 2) * snr**2 for k in ("ii", "iii")}          # noise-free, against (i)
        print(f"{line} S/N {snr:3d}: dchi2(ii) = {sig3(chi2['ii']):>6}   dchi2(iii) = {chi2['iii']:.2f}")
expected: (iii)'s smooth extra velocity from the matching condition: dv = 5.9883 km/s
python.note: the matching condition is closed form; the lines are summed over each clump's sub-cells, with no closed form, so that (iii) matches (i) is computed, not assumed

import numpy as np
from scipy.special import wofz

sigma_v = 2.6540e-2 * 0.4164 * 1215.6701e-8 / 1e5       # (pi e^2 / m_e c) f lambda0: cm^2 km/s
gamma = 6.2649e8 * 1215.6701e-8 / (4 * np.pi) / 1e5      # natural half width, km/s

def tau(u, u0, N, b):
    """one contribution: N sigma_v phi(u - u0), phi = H(a, x) / (sqrt(pi) b) with x = (u - u0)/b, a = gamma/b"""
    return N * sigma_v * wofz((u - u0) / b + 1j * gamma / b).real / (np.sqrt(np.pi) * b)

cells = [(-20.0, 5e13, 15.0), (0.0, 1e14, 20.0), (25.0, 3e13, 12.0)]   # (u0 km/s, N cm^-2, b km/s)
for u in (0.0, 20.0):
    each = [tau(u, *c) for c in cells]
    total = sum(each)
    print(f"u = {u:4.0f} km/s: tau = " + " + ".join(f"{t:.4f}" for t in each) + f" = {total:.4f};  F = exp(-tau) = {np.exp(-total):.5f} = product of exp(-tau_j) = {np.prod(np.exp(-np.array(each))):.5f}")
